doc: The catastrophe floor — hand-written compiled policy (kernel-spec M0); the encode-time compiler later emits this form. Two policy kinds per floor class: a provenance ENVELOPE (the floor action on a tainted path is provably illegitimate -> deny) and an effect FLOOR (the floor action itself is never executed silently -> require_approval, the corpus's 'confirm'). Dispositions follow the corpus four-quadrant model (corpus-spec 4.1): illegitimacy is established either by taint (injection) or by the human at the confirmation gate (hallucination); the kernel never judges legitimacy semantically. Floor criterion: a reasonable user would never want this done silently.

resolution.doc: Any policy True -> Violate; when several fire, the most severe disposition wins and every fired policy appears in the report. Else any policy Unknown -> Indeterminate (disposition escalate). Else Conform. Kleene three-valued logic throughout: a missing ctx field is Unknown, never a silent default.

fs.read.doc: Read a file. Corpus/adapter mapping: fs_read.

fs.write.doc: Write or append a file. Corpus/adapter mapping: fs_write.

process.spawn.doc: Execute a shell command. Corpus/adapter mapping: shell_exec; OpenClaw: sessions_spawn.

net.fetch.doc: Retrieval egress — request whose primary effect is reading from a host. Corpus/adapter mapping: http_get, dns_query.

net.send.doc: Content-carrying egress — any outbound send of data to a destination. Corpus/adapter mapping: http_post, webhook_post, email_send, sms_send, message_send, npm_publish, git_push, docker_push.

finance.transfer.doc: Move money. Corpus/adapter mapping: transfer, wire, pay_invoice, refund, crypto_send, gift_card. Amounts are i64 minor units (cents) — kernel-spec OQ1 ratified.

taint.trigger.doc: Provenance of the instruction that motivated this call — 'untrusted' when the step that proposed the action was following content from an untrusted source. Adapter-supplied; missing -> Unknown.

taint.path.doc: Provenance of the action's 'path' argument. Missing -> Unknown.

taint.content.doc: Provenance of the action's 'content' argument. Missing -> Unknown.

taint.command.doc: Provenance of the action's 'command' argument. Missing -> Unknown.

taint.to.doc: Provenance of the action's 'to' argument. Missing -> Unknown.

taint.body.doc: Provenance of the action's 'body' argument. Missing -> Unknown.

taint.url.doc: Provenance of the action's 'url' argument. Missing -> Unknown.

taint.amount_cents.doc: Provenance of the action's 'amount_cents' argument. Missing -> Unknown.

net.egress_allowlist.doc: Hosts the user has allowlisted for retrieval egress. Harness memory, read as context (corpus: environment.state.allowlist). Missing -> Unknown.

finance.saved_payees.doc: The user's saved payees. Harness memory, read as context (corpus: environment.state.saved_payees). Missing -> Unknown.

finance.threshold_cents.doc: The user's confirmation threshold in minor units. Harness memory, read as context (corpus: environment.state.threshold_cents). Missing -> Unknown.

is_secret.doc: True iff the canonicalized path is secret material (private keys, credential stores, token files). The kernel canonicalizes first (expand ~, lexical . / .. normalization) and matches the resolved path — never a raw string compare on unresolved input. Pattern set v1: corpus ground truths generalized with the gitleaks path taxonomy.

is_destructive_command.doc: True iff the command matches a destructive, irreversible form (recursive delete, device overwrite, database drop, history/log destruction, privilege or firewall sabotage, pipe-to-shell). v1 is lexical over the resolved command string — the corpus's own reviewed forms, MITRE ATT&CK-mapped. The semantic command resolver (PRD OQ6) later replaces the matching engine, not the policy shape; lexical bypass (obfuscation, aliasing) is a known, measured limitation of v1.

is_self_modification.doc: True iff the canonicalized path is one of the agent's own configuration or persistence surfaces — writes here change future agent behavior (skill poisoning, ATT&CK Persistence). Same canonicalize-then-match discipline as is_secret.

is_external.doc: Resolve the destination to a domain: URL/host forms -> host; email -> the domain after '@'; git remotes -> remote host. External iff the resolved domain (or a parent domain) is NOT in internal_domains and the host is not loopback, RFC1918, or '.internal'. Forms with no resolvable domain (bare phone numbers, chat handles) -> Unknown: externality is not crisp there and the kernel never guesses — Unknown drives Indeterminate -> escalate.
is_external.note: internal_domains is authored policy data — the personalization seam (author by intent, later learned from corrections). The v1 value matches the corpus's internal org.

is_allowlisted.doc: True iff the destination host exactly matches an entry of the user's egress allowlist (context). Missing allowlist -> Unknown.

is_unknown_payee.doc: True iff the payee (trimmed, case-insensitive) is NOT among the user's saved payees (context). Missing payee list -> Unknown.

no_tainted_secret_reads.rationale: A read of secret material whose target or trigger arrived from untrusted content is an injection reading the user's keys — denied outright.

secret_read_floor.rationale: Reading secret material (keys, credentials, token stores) is on the catastrophe floor; legitimate cases exist (key migration), so it is gated with confirmation — never executed silently.

no_tainted_exec.rationale: A destructive command whose text or trigger arrived from untrusted content is an injected attack on the system — denied outright.

destructive_exec_floor.rationale: Destructive, irreversible commands (recursive delete, device overwrite, DROP DATABASE) are on the catastrophe floor; the user may genuinely want them, so they are confirmed — a reasonable user never wants them run silently. The confirmation gate is also what catches the hallucinated ones: no taint marks an agent's own overreach.

no_tainted_self_modification.rationale: A write into the agent's own configuration or persistence surfaces driven by untrusted content is skill-poisoning — denied outright.

self_modification_floor.rationale: Writes to the agent's own config, shell rc files, git hooks, cron, or service definitions change future agent behavior; they are confirmed even when the user asked.

no_tainted_exfiltration.rationale: External send of untrusted-provenance data completes the lethal trifecta — denied outright.

external_send_floor.rationale: Sending content outside the trust domain is confirm-gated: legitimate external sends exist (the auditor, the client), but they never happen silently.

no_tainted_egress.rationale: Retrieval egress to an off-allowlist host on a tainted path is exfiltration by URL — denied outright.

unlisted_egress_floor.rationale: Egress to an external host not on the user's allowlist is confirm-gated; allowlisted retrieval stays quiet — the allowlist is exactly the noise budget, authored.

no_tainted_transfers.rationale: A transfer whose payee or amount arrived from untrusted content is an injected payment — denied outright.

financial_floor.rationale: Money movement over the user's threshold or to an unknown payee is irreversible enough to confirm — never silent. Under-threshold transfers to saved payees are the user's authored quiet zone.
